To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) imitation learning and structured prediction problems can be seen as no-regret online learning, (b) this leads to a new algorithm for imitation learning and structured sequence labeling that is simple and easy to implement, (c) the algorithm performs well empirically and (d) it is competitive with state-of-the-art methods.
(1) imitation learning and structured prediction are sequential prediction problems, and (2) a reduction of these to online learning leads to a new algorithm that outperforms existing approaches.

we introduce a new iterative algorithm that trains a stationary deterministic imitation policy, and that this new approach is more effective on imitation learning and structured prediction than previous approaches.

the problem of learning a structured policy in an imitation learning problem.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new algorithm proposed in this paper outperforms previous algorithms for imitation learning, which was one of the main goals of this paper.
the new algorithm outperforms previous ones on two imitation learning tasks and a benchmark structured prediction task, and is more general.
the proposed approach provides a new and promising way to solve sequential learning problems, such as imitation learning and structured prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new reduction from imitation learning and structured prediction to no-regret online learning and show that any algorithm satisfying this reduction must find a good policy.

we show how to reduce sequential prediction problems such as structured prediction and imitation learning to a no-regret online learning setting, and that any such no-regret algorithm can be used to find a policy with strong performance under the induced distribution.
we show a reduction from imitation learning to no-regret online learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under some assumptions, imitation learning and structured prediction problems reduce to no-regret online learning.
no regret online learning is a useful framework for sequential prediction problems.
no-regret online learning is a powerful tool to solve sequential prediction problems, and that the reduction we propose is a promising approach to tackle such sequential problems.
